rules.quote: The timer module provides a configurable number of 64-bit counters where each counter increments by a step value whenever the prescaler times out.
rules.condition: whenever the prescaler times out
rules.statement: Each 64-bit counter increments by the step value whenever the prescaler times out.

rules.quote: Each timer generates an interrupt if the counter reaches (or is above) a programmed value.
rules.condition: when the counter reaches or is above the programmed compare value
rules.statement: Each timer generates an interrupt if its counter reaches or exceeds the programmed value.

rules.quote: The timer IP provides memory-mapped registers equivalent to mtime and mtimecmp which can be used as the machine-mode timer registers defined in the RISC-V privileged spec.
rules.statement: The timer IP provides memory-mapped registers equivalent to mtime and mtimecmp usable as the RISC-V machine-mode timer registers.

rules.quote: A tick generator creates a tick every time its internal counter hits the CFG0.prescaler value.
rules.condition: when the tick generator's internal counter hits the CFG0.prescaler value
rules.statement: The tick generator creates a tick every time its internal counter hits the CFG0.prescaler value.

rules.quote: The tick is used to increment mtime by the CFG0.step value.
rules.condition: on each tick
rules.statement: Each tick increments mtime by the CFG0.step value.

rules.quote: The 64-bit mtime value is compared with the 64-bit mtimecmp. If mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp, the timer raises an interrupt.
rules.condition: when the 64-bit mtime is greater than or equal to the 64-bit mtimecmp
rules.statement: The timer compares 64-bit mtime with 64-bit mtimecmp and raises an interrupt when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp.

rules.quote: The tick module inside the timer IP is used to generate a fixed period of pulse signal. This allows creation of a call-clock timer tick such as 1us or 10us regardless of the system clock period.
rules.statement: The tick generator produces a fixed-period pulse signal, enabling a timer tick such as 1us or 10us regardless of the system clock period.

rules.quote: In this version, the timer only supports a single fixed clock, so the firmware should change CFG0.prescaler appropriately.
rules.condition: because the timer supports only a single fixed clock in this version
rules.statement: Firmware should change CFG0.prescaler appropriately for the single fixed clock frequency to obtain the desired tick period.

rules.section_title: Configurable number of timers and harts
rules.quote: Each hart has a set of tick generator and counter. It means the timer IP has the same number of prescalers, steps, and mtime registers as the number of harts.
rules.statement: Each hart has its own tick generator and counter, so the number of prescaler, step, and mtime registers equals the number of harts.

rules.section_title: Configurable number of timers and harts
rules.quote: Each hart can have multiple sets of mtimecmp, comparator logic, and expire interrupt signals.
rules.statement: Each hart can have multiple sets of mtimecmp, comparator logic, and expire interrupt signals.

rules.section_title: Configurable number of timers and harts
rules.quote: This version of the IP is fixed to have one Hart and one Timer per Hart.
rules.condition: in this version of the IP
rules.statement: The IP is fixed to one hart and one timer per hart.

rules.section_title: Configurable number of timers and harts
rules.quote: It has separate interrupts per timer and a set of interrupt enable and state registers per Hart.
rules.statement: There are separate interrupts per timer and a set of interrupt enable and state registers per hart.

rules.quote: These two fields need to be stable to correctly increment the timer value.
rules.condition: while the timer is active and incrementing
rules.statement: The prescaler and step fields must be stable for the timer value to increment correctly.

rules.quote: If software wants to change these fields, it should de-activate the timer and then proceed.
rules.condition: when software wants to change prescaler or step
rules.statement: Software should de-activate the timer before changing the prescaler or step fields, then proceed with the change.

rules.quote: The CPU cannot access 64-bit data in a single request.
rules.statement: The CPU cannot access a 64-bit value in a single request over the 32-bit register interface; two 32-bit accesses are required.

rules.quote: However, when split into two reads, it is possible the timer value can increment between the two requests.
rules.condition: when a 64-bit timer value is read as two separate 32-bit reads
rules.statement: The timer value may increment between the two 32-bit reads of mtime and mtimeh.

rules.quote: This condition can be detected in a standard way using a third read.
rules.condition: when reading the 64-bit timer value in two reads
rules.statement: A rollover between the two reads can be detected in a standard way using a third read.

rules.quote: In typical usage the mtime register would not be written, but if there is a need to set it to an arbitrary, dynamically-determined value, the following sequence should be used to prevent the operation of the timer yielding an indeterminate result:
rules.condition: when mtime must be set to an arbitrary, dynamically-determined value
rules.statement: Software should use the prescribed safe write sequence to set mtime so timer operation does not yield an indeterminate result.

rules.quote: In the event that the target value of the lower half is close to 0xFFFF_FFFF, this sequence prevents the timer from assuming an incorrect time between the two 32-bit writes required to set the 64-bit timer value.
rules.condition: when the target lower half of mtime is close to 0xFFFF_FFFF
rules.statement: The safe write sequence should be used so the timer does not assume an incorrect time between the two 32-bit writes.

rules.quote: If the value of mtime is modified in this manner then mtimecmp shall be written after mtime in order to clear any pending interrupt condition.
rules.condition: when mtime is modified
rules.statement: mtimecmp shall be written after mtime in order to clear any pending interrupt condition.

rules.quote: With a CFG0.step above 1, one tick can also carry mtime from below mtimecmp past the end of the range, so mtime skips the comparison value and the interrupt is not raised.
rules.condition: when CFG0.step is above 1 and mtimecmp is close to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF
rules.statement: One tick can carry mtime from below mtimecmp past the end of the range, so mtime skips mtimecmp and the interrupt is not raised.

rules.quote: A possible solution is to have an intermediate interrupt by setting the mtimecmp to 64-bit all-ones, 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF.
rules.condition: when the computed mtime + timeout comparison value overflows
rules.statement: Software may set mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF to get an intermediate interrupt.

rules.quote: Then the service routine for that interrupt will need to poll mtime until it wraps (which could take up to a timer clock tick) before scheduling the required interrupt using the originally computed mtimecmp value.
rules.condition: in the service routine for the intermediate all-ones interrupt
rules.statement: The service routine needs to poll mtime until it wraps before scheduling the required interrupt with the originally computed mtimecmp value.

rules.quote: With a step above 1, mtime can step over the all-ones value and this intermediate interrupt is never raised.
rules.condition: when step is above 1
rules.statement: mtime can step over the all-ones value so the intermediate interrupt is never raised.

rules.quote: Setting mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF - step + 1 works for any nonzero step, since the last value of mtime before it wraps is always at least that large.
rules.condition: for any nonzero step
rules.statement: Setting mtimecmp to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF - step + 1 works for the intermediate interrupt, since the last mtime before wrap is at least that large.

rules.quote: If mtime is greater than or equal to the value of mtimecmp, the interrupt is generated from the RV_TIMER module.
rules.condition: when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp
rules.statement: The RV_TIMER module generates the interrupt when mtime is greater than or equal to mtimecmp.

rules.quote: Clearing the interrupt can be done by writing 1 into the Interrupt Status register INTR_STATE0.
rules.statement: The interrupt can be cleared by writing 1 to the Interrupt Status register INTR_STATE0.

rules.quote: The RV_TIMER module also follows RISC-V Privileged spec that requires the interrupt to be cleared by updating mtimecmp memory-mapped CSRs. In this case both COMPARE_LOWER0_0 and COMPARE_UPPER0_0 can clear the interrupt source.
rules.statement: The interrupt can be cleared by updating mtimecmp; a write to either COMPARE_LOWER0_0 or COMPARE_UPPER0_0 clears the interrupt source.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.ALERT_TEST; Offset: 0x0; Length: 4; Description: Alert Test Register Offset: 0x0
rules.statement: ALERT_TEST register must be located at offset 0x0 with length 4 bytes.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.CTRL; Offset: 0x4; Length: 4; Description: Control register Offset: 0x4 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0x1
rules.statement: CTRL must be at offset 0x4, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.INTR_ENABLE0; Offset: 0x100; Length: 4; Description: Interrupt Enable Offset: 0x100 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0x1
rules.statement: INTR_ENABLE0 must be at offset 0x100, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.INTR_STATE0; Offset: 0x104; Length: 4; Description: Interrupt Status Offset: 0x104 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0x1
rules.statement: INTR_STATE0 must be at offset 0x104, length 4, reset to 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.INTR_TEST0; Offset: 0x108; Length: 4; Description: Interrupt test register Offset: 0x108 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0x1
rules.statement: INTR_TEST0 must be at offset 0x108, length 4, reset value 0x0 with reset mask 0x1.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.CFG0; Offset: 0x10c; Length: 4; Description: Configuration for Hart 0 Offset: 0x10c Reset default: 0x10000 Reset mask: 0xff0fff
rules.statement: CFG0 must be at offset 0x10c, length 4, reset to 0x10000 with reset mask 0xff0fff.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.TIMER_V_LOWER0; Offset: 0x110; Length: 4; Description: Timer value Lower Offset: 0x110 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0xffffffff Bits: 31:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: v; Description: Timer value [31:0]
rules.statement: TIMER_V_LOWER0 at offset 0x110 holds timer value [31:0] as rw field v, reset 0x0, mask 0xffffffff.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.TIMER_V_UPPER0; Offset: 0x114; Length: 4; Description: Timer value Upper Offset: 0x114 Reset default: 0x0 Reset mask: 0xffffffff Bits: 31:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: v; Description: Timer value [63:32]
rules.statement: TIMER_V_UPPER0 at offset 0x114 holds timer value [63:32] as rw field v, reset 0x0, mask 0xffffffff.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.COMPARE_LOWER0_0; Offset: 0x118; Length: 4; Description: Timer value Lower Offset: 0x118 Reset default: 0xffffffff Reset mask: 0xffffffff Bits: 31:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0xffffffff; Name: v; Description: Timer compare value [31:0]
rules.statement: COMPARE_LOWER0_0 at offset 0x118 holds compare value [31:0] as rw field v, reset 0xffffffff, mask 0xffffffff.

rules.quote: Name: rv_timer.COMPARE_UPPER0_0; Offset: 0x11c; Length: 4; Description: Timer value Upper Offset: 0x11c Reset default: 0xffffffff Reset mask: 0xffffffff Bits: 31:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0xffffffff; Name: v; Description: Timer compare value [63:32]
rules.statement: COMPARE_UPPER0_0 at offset 0x11c holds compare value [63:32] as rw field v, reset 0xffffffff, mask 0xffffffff.

rules.quote: Reset default: 0x80000000 Reset mask: 0x80000001
rules.condition: After reset
rules.statement: ALERT_TEST must reset to 0x80000000 with reset mask 0x80000001.

rules.quote: Bits: 31; Type: rw0c; Reset: 0x1; Name: regwen; Description: Write 0 to disable alert testing until the next reset.
rules.condition: Software writes 0 to ALERT_TEST regwen bit 31 (rw0c, reset 0x1)
rules.statement: Writing 0 to regwen disables alert testing until the next reset; regwen can only be cleared, not set, by writes.

rules.quote: Bits: 30:1; Description: Reserved
rules.statement: ALERT_TEST bits 30:1 are reserved.

rules.quote: Bits: 0; Type: wo; Reset: 0x0; Name: fatal_fault; Description: Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.
rules.condition: Write 1 to ALERT_TEST bit 0 (wo, reset 0x0) while alert testing is enabled
rules.statement: Writing 1 to fatal_fault triggers one alert event of the fatal kind.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:1; Description: Reserved Bits: 0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: active_0; Description: If 1, timer operates
rules.condition: CTRL.active_0 (rw, reset 0x0) is 1
rules.statement: When active_0 is 1 the timer operates; bits 31:1 of CTRL are reserved.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:1; Description: Reserved Bits: 0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: IE_0; Description: Interrupt Enable for timer
rules.statement: IE_0 (bit 0, rw, reset 0x0) is the interrupt enable for the timer; bits 31:1 are reserved.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:1; Description: Reserved Bits: 0; Type: rw1c; Reset: 0x0; Name: IS_0; Description: Interrupt status for timer
rules.statement: IS_0 (bit 0, rw1c, reset 0x0) holds the timer interrupt status and is cleared by writing 1; bits 31:1 are reserved.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:1; Description: Reserved Bits: 0; Type: wo; Reset: x; Name: T_0; Description: Interrupt test for timer
rules.statement: T_0 (bit 0, wo, reset x) is the interrupt test for timer; bits 31:1 are reserved.

rules.quote: Bits: 31:24; Description: Reserved Bits: 23:16; Type: rw; Reset: 0x1; Name: step; Description: Incremental value for each tick Bits: 15:12; Description: Reserved Bits: 11:0; Type: rw; Reset: 0x0; Name: prescale; Description: Prescaler to generate tick
rules.statement: CFG0 step (bits 23:16, rw, reset 0x1) is the increment per tick; prescale (bits 11:0, rw, reset 0x0) generates the tick; other bits reserved.

rules.quote: Port Name: racl_policies; Package::Struct: top_racl_pkg::racl_policy_vec; Type: uni; Act: rcv; Width: 1; Description: Incoming RACL policy vector from a racl_ctrl instance. The policy selection vector (parameter) selects the policy for each register.
rules.statement: The racl_policies input must carry the incoming RACL policy vector from a racl_ctrl instance, with the policy selection vector parameter selecting the policy for each register.

rules.quote: Port Name: racl_error; Package::Struct: top_racl_pkg::racl_error_log; Type: uni; Act: req; Width: 1; Description: RACL error log information of this module.
rules.statement: The module must output RACL error log information of this module on racl_error.

rules.quote: Interrupt Name: timer_expired_hart0_timer0; Type: Event; Description: raised if hart0's timer0 expired (mtime >= mtimecmp)
rules.condition: hart0's timer0 expired (mtime >= mtimecmp)
rules.statement: The module must raise interrupt timer_expired_hart0_timer0 when hart0's timer0 has expired (mtime >= mtimecmp).

rules.quote: Alert Name: fatal_fault; Description: This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected inside the RV_TIMER unit.
rules.condition: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected inside the RV_TIMER unit
rules.statement: The fatal_fault alert must be triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is detected inside RV_TIMER.

rules.quote: Countermeasure ID: RV_TIMER.BUS.INTEGRITY; Description: End-to-end bus integrity scheme.
rules.statement: The module must implement the RV_TIMER.BUS.INTEGRITY countermeasure, an end-to-end bus integrity scheme on the TL-UL interface.

rules.section_title: ot_rv_timer_nnc: integration of the OpenTitan rv_timer for verification
rules.quote: This document describes the verification top ot_rv_timer_nnc: the OpenTitan rv_timer (specified by the OpenTitan parts of this document, above) plus a thin wrapper that flattens its struct ports and closes two protocols.
rules.statement: The verification top ot_rv_timer_nnc must consist of the OpenTitan rv_timer plus a thin wrapper that flattens its struct ports and closes two protocols.

rules.section_title: ot_rv_timer_nnc: integration of the OpenTitan rv_timer for verification
rules.quote: The behaviour of rv_timer itself is specified only by the OpenTitan documents; this document adds the port mapping, the fixed configuration and what the wrapper does.
rules.statement: The behaviour of rv_timer itself must follow only the OpenTitan documents; the wrapper adds only port mapping, fixed configuration and wrapper behaviour.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-001] The design under verification has one hart and one timer (N_HARTS = 1, N_TIMERS = 1), as stated in the rv_timer Features and Theory of Operation sections.
rules.statement: The design under verification has exactly one hart and one timer (N_HARTS = 1, N_TIMERS = 1).

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-002] RACL (register access control) is disabled: every register access is permitted, and no access is rejected for an access-control reason.
rules.condition: RACL is disabled
rules.statement: Every register access is permitted when RACL is disabled.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-002] RACL (register access control) is disabled: every register access is permitted, and no access is rejected for an access-control reason.
rules.condition: RACL is disabled
rules.statement: No register access is rejected for an access-control reason.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-003] The alert sender of rv_timer and the alert receiver of the wrapper both use the synchronous clocking scheme (no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs).
rules.statement: The alert sender of rv_timer and the alert receiver of the wrapper both use the synchronous clocking scheme, with no synchronizer flops on the differential pairs.

rules.quote: Ping requests are never issued.
rules.statement: Alert ping requests are never issued.

rules.quote: [INT-CFG-004] There is no design parameter to vary: every run uses this one configuration.
rules.statement: Every run uses the single fixed configuration; there is no design parameter to vary.

rules.quote: [INT-CLK-001] clk_i is the only clock.
rules.statement: clk_i is the only clock in the design.

rules.quote: All inputs are sampled and all outputs change at its rising edge, except for the effect of rst_ni.
rules.statement: All inputs are sampled and all outputs change at the rising edge of clk_i, except for the effect of rst_ni.

rules.quote: [INT-RST-001] rst_ni is the active-low reset, asserted asynchronously and released synchronously to clk_i (the reset strategy of the comportability specification).
rules.statement: rst_ni is active-low and may be asserted asynchronously, but its release must be synchronous to clk_i.

rules.quote: While rst_ni is 0, every register holds its reset value as given in the register tables of the rv_timer specification.
rules.condition: While rst_ni is 0
rules.statement: Every register holds its reset value as given in the rv_timer specification register tables.

rules.quote: Port: i_a_opcode; Direction: input; Width: 3; Meaning: TL-UL a_opcode (Get = 4, PutFullData = 0, PutPartialData = 1)
rules.statement: i_a_opcode must encode TL-UL request types as Get = 4, PutFullData = 0 and PutPartialData = 1.

rules.quote: Port: i_a_instr; Direction: input; Width: 1; Meaning: 1: the request is an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); 0: a data access (MuBi4False)
rules.statement: i_a_instr = 1 marks the request as an instruction fetch (a_user.instr_type = MuBi4True); i_a_instr = 0 marks a data access (MuBi4False).

rules.quote: Port: i_a_intg_flip; Direction: input; Width: 1; Meaning: 1: the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted (see 4.2)
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip is 1
rules.statement: When i_a_intg_flip is 1, the A-channel integrity sent with the request is corrupted.

rules.quote: Port: o_d_opcode; Direction: output; Width: 3; Meaning: TL-UL d_opcode (AccessAck = 0, AccessAckData = 1)
rules.statement: o_d_opcode must encode TL-UL response types as AccessAck = 0 and AccessAckData = 1.

rules.quote: Port: o_d_intg_err; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong (see 4.3)
rules.condition: the response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong
rules.statement: o_d_intg_err indicates that the response integrity of the D-channel beat is wrong.

rules.quote: Port: o_alert; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Alert fatal_fault received (see 5)
rules.condition: alert fatal_fault is received
rules.statement: o_alert indicates that the alert fatal_fault was received.

rules.quote: Port: o_alert_integ_fail; Direction: output; Width: 1; Meaning: Signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs (see 5)
rules.condition: a signal integrity failure occurs on the alert differential pairs
rules.statement: o_alert_integ_fail indicates a signal integrity failure on the alert differential pairs.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-001] The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports are the fields of the same name of the TL-UL device interface tl of rv_timer, with the meaning given by the TL-UL bus specification.
rules.statement: The i_a_*, o_a_ready, o_d_* (except o_d_intg_err) and i_d_ready ports must be the same-named fields of the rv_timer TL-UL device interface tl, with TL-UL meaning.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-002] a_user.rsvd is 0. a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when it is 0.
rules.statement: a_user.rsvd is 0.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-002] a_user.rsvd is 0. a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when it is 0.
rules.statement: a_user.instr_type is MuBi4True when i_a_instr is 1 and MuBi4False when i_a_instr is 0.

rules.quote: [INT-TL-003] The test bench acts as the TL-UL host. It shall follow the host rules of the TL-UL bus specification (for example, the A-channel signals stay stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0).
rules.condition: test bench acting as TL-UL host
rules.statement: The test bench must follow the TL-UL host rules, including keeping A-channel signals stable while a_valid is 1 and a_ready is 0.

rules.quote: Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus: the device answers them with d_error = 1 as the specifications require.
rules.statement: The test bench may send requests listed as TL-UL error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) as legal stimulus.

rules.quote: Requests that the TL-UL specification lists as error cases (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address) are legal stimulus: the device answers them with d_error = 1 as the specifications require.
rules.condition: request is a TL-UL error case (unsupported opcode, bad size or mask, misaligned address)
rules.statement: The device must answer such error-case requests with d_error = 1.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-001] The wrapper computes a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg of every request with OpenTitan's integrity generator for TL-UL hosts (the section Bus Integrity Scheme of the TL-UL bus specification is not written yet; the code is not part of this specification). A request with i_a_intg_flip = 0 therefore always carries correct integrity, and the test bench does not compute integrity itself.
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip = 0
rules.statement: The wrapper must compute a_user.cmd_intg and a_user.data_intg with the OpenTitan TL-UL host integrity generator, so the request carries correct integrity.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-002] When i_a_intg_flip is 1, bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg is inverted.
rules.condition: i_a_intg_flip is 1
rules.statement: Bit 0 of a_user.cmd_intg must be inverted.

rules.quote: The request then has a command integrity error: a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault in the sense of the rv_timer Security Alerts table, which triggers the fatal_fault alert (section 5).
rules.condition: request has command integrity error (i_a_intg_flip is 1)
rules.statement: Such a request is a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault that triggers the fatal_fault alert.

rules.quote: [INT-INTG-003] The wrapper checks d_user.rsp_intg of every D-channel beat against the response fields with OpenTitan's response integrity checker for TL-UL hosts. o_d_intg_err is 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and this check fails, and 0 otherwise.
rules.statement: o_d_intg_err must be 1 in a cycle where o_d_valid is 1 and the d_user.rsp_intg check fails, and 0 otherwise.

rules.quote: A correct device never makes it 1.
rules.statement: A correct device must never make o_d_intg_err 1.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-001] rv_timer has one alert, fatal_fault, sent through an alert sender.
rules.statement: rv_timer has one alert, fatal_fault, sent through an alert sender.

rules.quote: The wrapper connects it to an alert receiver as described in the alert handler theory of operation (Differential Alert Signaling). o_alert is the alert_o output of that receiver: it is 1 for one clock cycle for each alert handshake that the receiver detects.
rules.condition: When the alert receiver detects an alert handshake
rules.statement: o_alert is the receiver's alert_o output and is 1 for one clock cycle for each alert handshake the receiver detects.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-002] o_alert_integ_fail is the integ_fail_o output of the receiver.
rules.statement: o_alert_integ_fail is the integ_fail_o output of the alert receiver.

rules.quote: A correct sender never makes it 1.
rules.condition: With a correct alert sender
rules.statement: A correct sender never makes o_alert_integ_fail 1.

rules.quote: [INT-ALERT-003] A fatal alert is repeated until reset (comportability specification, Alerts per Module), so after a bus integrity fault o_alert pulses repeatedly until rst_ni is asserted.
rules.condition: After a bus integrity fault, until rst_ni is asserted
rules.statement: o_alert pulses repeatedly after a bus integrity fault until rst_ni is asserted, as a fatal alert is repeated until reset.

rules.quote: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers one alert event, as the register description says.
rules.condition: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault
rules.statement: A write of 1 to ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault triggers exactly one alert event.

rules.quote: [INT-INTR-001] o_intr_timer_expired is the interrupt output intr_timer_expired_hart0_timer0_o of rv_timer, an event-type interrupt as defined in the comportability specification, with the registers INTR_ENABLE0, INTR_STATE0 and INTR_TEST0.
rules.statement: o_intr_timer_expired must be the interrupt output intr_timer_expired_hart0_timer0_o of rv_timer.

rules.quote: [INT-INTR-001] o_intr_timer_expired is the interrupt output intr_timer_expired_hart0_timer0_o of rv_timer, an event-type interrupt as defined in the comportability specification, with the registers INTR_ENABLE0, INTR_STATE0 and INTR_TEST0.
rules.statement: o_intr_timer_expired must behave as an event-type interrupt per the comportability specification, with registers INTR_ENABLE0, INTR_STATE0 and INTR_TEST0.

rules.quote: [INT-VER-001] The verification shall cover, through the ports above: reset values of every register; the access type of every register field as given in the register tables (rw, rw1c, wo, rw0c); the tick generator (prescaler) and the step; counting of the 64-bit timer value, including writes to it and the carry from the lower to the upper half; the compare and the interrupt (state, enable, test, clearing by writing the compare registers); ALERT_TEST with its regwen field; bus error responses (unmapped addresses, sub-word writes, instruction fetches, integrity errors) and the fatal_fault alert.
rules.statement: Verification shall cover reset values of every register through the ports.

rules.quote: [INT-VER-001] The verification shall cover, through the ports above: reset values of every register; the access type of every register field as given in the register tables (rw, rw1c, wo, rw0c); the tick generator (prescaler) and the step; counting of the 64-bit timer value, including writes to it and the carry from the lower to the upper half; the compare and the interrupt (state, enable, test, clearing by writing the compare registers); ALERT_TEST with its regwen field; bus error responses (unmapped addresses, sub-word writes, instruction fetches, integrity errors) and the fatal_fault alert.
rules.statement: Verification shall cover the access type of every register field as given in the register tables (rw, rw1c, wo, rw0c).

rules.quote: ID: D-001; Question: Tick period (gaps 004, 005; question 1); Decision: With CTRL.active_0 = 1 and CFG0 unchanged, the timer value increases by CFG0.step (modulo 2^64) once every CFG0.prescale + 1 cycles (the 48 MHz example: prescale 47 gives a tick every 48 cycles), so prescale 0 gives a tick every cycle. The cycle of the first tick after active_0 becomes 1 is not specified; it shall come no later than CFG0.prescale + 1 + 4 cycles after the write response.
rules.condition: CTRL.active_0 = 1 and CFG0 unchanged
rules.statement: Timer value increases by CFG0.step (modulo 2^64) once every CFG0.prescale + 1 cycles; prescale 0 gives a tick every cycle.

rules.statement: Tests write CFG0 and TIMER_V_* only while CTRL.active_0 = 0; behaviour after such a write while active is not checked.

While the condition holds and the timer is active, INTR_STATE0.IS_0 shall read 1 within 4 cycles after a write of 1 to it.

skipped.text: This document specifies RISC-V Timer hardware IP functionality.
This module conforms to the Comportable guideline for peripheral functionality.
See that document for integration overview within the broader top level system.
64-bit timer with 12-bit prescaler and 8-bit step register
Compliant with RISC-V privileged specification v1.11
Configurable number of timers per hart and number of harts
Note: Although the number of timers is indeed configurable, the implementation currently only connects up one timer for one hart.
The timer is intended to be used by the processors to check the current time relative to the reset or the system power-on.
In this version, the timer doesn't consider low-power modes and assumes the clock is neither turned off nor changed during runtime.
Additional features such as prescaler, step, and a configurable number of timers and harts have been added.
The timer module is composed of tick generators, counters, and comparators.
It is useful if the system has more than one clock as a clock source.
The firmware just needs to adjust the CFG0.prescaler value and the actual timer interrupt handling routine does not need a variable clock period to update mtimecmp.
For instance, if a system switches between 48MHz and 200MHz clocks, a prescaler value of 47 for 48MHz and 199 for 200MHz will generate a 1us tick.
The timer IP supports more than one HART and/or more than one timer per hart.
Below is an example configuration file for N_TIMER 2 and N_HARTS 2.
Software is expected to configure prescaler and step before activating the timer.
The timer IP has 64-bit timer value registers and 64-bit compare registers.
The register interface, however, is set to 32-bit data width.
The IP doesn't have a latching or blocking mechanism to avoid this issue.
It is the programmer's responsibility to ensure the correct value is read.

For instance, if the CPU reads 0xFFFF_FFFF from lower 32-bit timer value (mtime) and 0x0000_0001 from upper 32-bit timer value (mtimeh), there is a chance that rather than having the value 0x1_FFFF_FFFF the timer value has changed from 0x0_FFFF_FFFF to 0x1_0000_0000 between the two reads.
If there is the possibility of an interrupt between the two reads then the counter could have advanced even more.
Figure 10.1 in the RISC-V unprivileged specification explains how to avoid this.
Updating mtimecmp register also follows a similar approach to avoid a spurious interrupt during the register update.
Please refer to the mtimecmp section in the RISC-V privileged specification.
There are some peculiarities when mtime and mtimecmp get close to the end of the 64-bit integer range.
In particular, because an unsigned comparison is done between mtime and mtimecmp care is needed.
A couple of cases are:
mtimecmp close to 0xFFFF_FFFF_FFFF_FFFF.

In this case the time-out event will be signaled when mtime passes the comparison value, the interrupt will be raised and the source indicated in the corresponding bit of the interrupt status register.

However, if there is a delay in servicing the interrupt the mtime value could wrap to zero (and continue to increment) so the value read by the interrupt service routine will be less than the comparison value.
When the timer is setup to trigger a timeout some number of timer ticks into the future, the computation of the comparison value mtime + timeout may overflow.
If this value is set in mtimecmp it would make mtime greater than mtimecmp and immediately signal an interrupt.
If the core enables the timer interrupt in MIE CSR, it jumps into the timer interrupt service routine.

These decisions answer questions that the documents above leave open (gaps found by nnc spec-lint before gate G1, and the open questions of the rule review).
They were made by Claude on the delegation of the project owner (GabrielHCMUT), on 2026-11-20, from the documents only; they are not OpenTitan requirements and not a hardware designer's review.
Where the documents do not decide a behaviour, the decision is that the verification does not demand one reading: it checks only what every reading has in common, or a bound.
The numeric bounds in this section are verification bounds chosen to be generous, not timing requirements of rv_timer.
ID: D-004; Question: Expiry while inactive (gap 003); Decision: Not specified. INTR_STATE0 and the interrupt are not checked while CTRL.active_0 = 0 with mtime >= mtimecmp.

ID: D-007; Question: Software write to INTR_STATE0 at the same time as an expiry (question 17); Decision: Software has precedence for that cycle; if the condition still holds, IS_0 returns to 1 (register tool, simultaneous access). Only the result after 4 cycles is checked.

ID: D-020; Question: Access type of INTR_STATE0.IS_0 (gap 014); Decision: The register tables bind: IS_0 is rw1c. The hjson text in the Theory of Operation is an example for two harts and two timers, not this configuration.
